name: Hanan
overview: Hanan was a male figure in the Old Testament known primarily as the son of Maacah and Joshaphat the Mithnite. His tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded in Scripture beyond this lineage. There are no additional notes or details about his life provided in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Hanan means 'gracious' in Hebrew. It is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 11:43, but it is not indicated that this name was given by God or carries a divine title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hanan was the son of Maacah and also the son of Joshaphat the Mithnite, as noted in 1 Chronicles 11:43. No other family relationships are mentioned.
scriptureSignificance: Hanan's significance in the biblical narrative is tied to his identification within the genealogical records of Israel, specifically as a descendant of Joshaphat the Mithnite. His mention in 1 Chronicles 11:43 places him among the figures associated with the early history of King David's reign, providing insight into the individuals who were part of that historical context. While not a prominent character with recorded deeds, his inclusion underscores the detailed preservation of lineage in Scripture.
